t.1.65.1: Then, at clear daybreak, the king of men, having performed his morning rites, summoned the great-souled Viśvāmitra together with Rāghava.
t.1.65.2: Having honored him and the two great-souled Rāghavas with rites as prescribed in the śāstras, the righteous-souled one then spoke these words.
t.1.65.3: O blessed one, may you be welcome! What may I do for you, O sinless one? Let your honour command me, for I am to be commanded by you.
t.1.65.4: Thus addressed by the great-souled Janaka, that righteous sage, skilled in speech, replied to the hero with these words.
t.1.65.5: These two sons of Daśaratha, kṣatriyas renowned throughout the world, wish to see that excellent bow which rests with you.
t.1.65.6: Show this to them, may good fortune be yours; having seen this bow, the two princes will have their wish fulfilled and will return as they please.
t.1.65.7: Thus addressed, Janaka replied to the great sage: "Let it be heard for what purpose this bow stands here."
t.1.65.8: There was a king, sixth in descent from Nimi, known as Devarāta. This sacred trust was placed in his hands by the great-souled one.
t.1.65.9: Long ago, at the destruction of Dakṣa's sacrifice, the mighty Rudra, having drawn his bow, spoke these words to the gods in anger and derision.
t.1.65.10: Since you, O gods, eager for shares yourselves, did not allot shares to me, I shall cut off your excellent and most precious limbs with my bow.
t.1.65.11: Then, O best of sages, all the gods, downcast, sought to appease the lord of the gods, and Bhava became pleased with them.
t.1.65.13: This, O lord, is that jewel of a bow belonging to the great-souled God of gods, which was then deposited as a trust with our forefather.
t.1.65.14: Then, as I was ploughing the field, a girl rose up from the plough; found by me while I was clearing the field, she is renowned by the name Sītā.
t.1.65.12: Filled with joy, he gave to all those great-souled ones.
t.1.65.15: She who rose up from the surface of the earth grew up as my daughter. This maiden of mine, not born from a womb, has been set aside as one whose bride-price is valor.
t.1.65.16: O bull among sages, as that daughter of mine, who had risen from the surface of the earth, was growing up, kings came and sought her hand in marriage.
t.1.65.17: O blessed one, to all those kings who came seeking the maiden's hand, I did not give my daughter, for she is one whose bride-price is valour.
t.1.65.18: Then, O bull among sages, all the kings assembled together and came to Mithilā, eager at that time to put the strength to the test.
t.1.65.19: For them, as they sought to test its strength, the bow was brought forth; yet they were not able to grasp that bow, nor even to lift it.
t.1.65.20: Knowing that the strength of those mighty kings was slight, O great sage, I turned them away. Understand this, O you whose wealth is austerity.
t.1.65.21: Then, O bull among sages, all the kings, their prowess having been called into doubt, laid siege to Mithilā in supreme wrath.
t.1.65.22: Realizing that they had been rejected, O bull among sages, they were seized by a great fury and laid siege to the city of Mithilā.
t.1.65.24: Then by my austerity I propitiated all the hosts of gods, and the gods, supremely pleased, gave me a fourfold army.
t.1.65.23: Then, when a full year had passed, my resources were exhausted in every respect, O best of sages, and so I became deeply distressed.
t.1.65.25: Then the kings, routed and being slain, fled in all directions together with their ministers, those evildoers, powerless, their valor now in doubt.
t.1.65.26: O tiger among sages, O you of excellent vows, I shall show this supremely radiant bow to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as well.
t.1.65.27: O sage, if Rāma can string this bow, I shall give my daughter Sītā, who was not born of a womb, to the son of Daśaratha.
